title: 36 Questions That Lead to Love
questions: Given the choice of anyone in the world, whom would you want as a dinner guest?
Would you like to be famous? In what way?
Before making a telephone call, do you ever rehearse what you are going to say? Why?
What would constitute a “perfect” day for you?
When did you last sing to yourself? To someone else?
If you were able to live to the age of 90 and retain either the mind or body of a 30-year-old for the last 60 years of your life, which would you want?
Do you have a secret hunch about how you will die?
Name three things you and your partner appear to have in common.
For what in your life do you feel most grateful?
If you could change anything about the way you were raised, what would it be?
Take four minutes and tell your partner your life story in as much detail as possible.
If you could wake up tomorrow having gained any one quality or ability, what would it be?
If a crystal ball could tell you the truth about yourself, your life, the future or anything else, what would you want to know?
Is there something that you’ve dreamed of doing for a long time? Why haven’t you done it?
What is the greatest accomplishment of your life?
What do you value most in a friendship?
What is your most treasured memory?
What is your most terrible memory?
If you knew that in one year you would die suddenly, would you change anything about the way you are now living? Why?
What does friendship mean to you?
What roles do love and affection play in your life?
Alternate sharing something you consider a positive characteristic of your partner. Share a total of five items.
How close and warm is your family? Do you feel your childhood was happier than most other people’s?
How do you feel about your relationship with your mother?
Make three true “we” statements each. For instance, “We are both in this room feeling ... “
Complete this sentence: “I wish I had someone with whom I could share ... “
If you were going to become a close friend with your partner, please share what would be important for him or her to know.
Tell your partner what you like about them; be very honest this time, saying things that you might not say to someone you’ve just met.
Share with your partner an embarrassing moment in your life.
When did you last cry in front of another person? By yourself?
Tell your partner something that you like about them already.
What, if anything, is too serious to be joked about?
If you were to die this evening with no opportunity to communicate with anyone, what would you most regret not having told someone? Why haven’t you told them yet?
Your house, containing everything you own, catches fire. After saving your loved ones and pets, you have time to safely make a final dash to save any one item. What would it be? Why?
Of all the people in your family, whose death would you find most disturbing? Why?
Share a personal problem and ask your partner’s advice on how he or she might handle it. Also, ask your partner to reflect back to you how you seem to be feeling about the problem you have chosen.

title: 36 Questions That Spark Creativity
questions: If this cafe were a scene in a movie, what kind of movie would it be?
What’s a book or film you wish you could experience again for the first time?
Do you usually root for the hero, or do you secretly enjoy a really well-written villain?
What kind of story do you think you’re living in right now—genre-wise?
What makes a romance story actually believable to you?
Do you prefer plot-twist endings or slow, emotional ones that stay with you?
What’s a book or film everyone loves but you’re just… not that into?
As a law graduate—do courtroom dramas impress you or make you cringe?
What kind of characters do you always end up caring about, no matter the story?
What’s something you’ve really enjoyed about getting to know someone slowly?
If this cafe existed inside a novel, what genre would it be—and who would we be in the story?
If you could live inside one fictional city for a year, which one would you choose?
If your life suddenly turned into a film, would it be more dialogue-driven or action-driven?
If you had to give today a title, what would it be?
If you could instantly know the truth about one mystery—real or fictional—what would you choose?
If you had to defend a fictional character in court, who would you choose and why?
If a villain genuinely believes they’re right, do you think that makes them more dangerous—or more human?
If you could rewrite the ending of any book or film, would you change it or leave it painful on purpose?
If you were forced to live one story trope for a year—friends-to-lovers, found family, chosen one, or rivals—what would you pick?
If you could only read one genre for the next five years, which would survive the cut?
If the law and justice ever clearly conflicted, which one should win?
If someone commits a crime for a genuinely good reason, do you think that changes who they are?
If you had absolute certainty someone would do something terrible in the future, would stopping them now be fair?
If memory could be used as evidence in court, would that make the world better—or scarier?
If you could freeze one kind of moment in life and relive it whenever you want, what kind would it be?
If you suddenly had a year off with no consequences, how do you think you’d change?
If someone understood you perfectly but challenged you constantly, would that feel comforting or exhausting?
If you could ask your future self one question and get an honest answer, what would you ask?
If two people meet at the wrong time but are right for each other, do you think timing can be fixed?
If a connection feels easy but deep at the same time, do you think that’s rare—or something people overlook?
If you were writing a crime novel, would you rather be the detective, the criminal, or the observer who knows everything?
If a book perfectly captured this phase of your life, would it be hopeful, tense, or quietly reflective?
If you could step into any story just to change one small decision, would you do it?
If a film was made about two people slowly getting closer, what would matter more—chemistry or timing?
If you had to describe your inner world as a genre, which one fits best?
If tonight ended exactly the way it’s supposed to, what kind of ending would it be?

title: IELTS P2 - 13 People Questions
questions: Describe a member of your family you get on well with. You should say: who it is, what relationship you have to that person, what that person is like, what you do together, and explain why you get on so well.
Describe a person you know who is kind. You should say: who it is, how you know this person, what sort of person he/she is, and explain why you think they are kind.
Describe an old person you know. You should say: who this person is, how old he/she is, what this person is like, and explain why you like this person.
Describe someone you respect. You should say: who the person is, how you know about this person, what this person does, what this person is like, and explain why you respect this person.
Describe a Person Who Inspired You. You should say: who the person is, how you know him or her, what qualities you admire, and explain why this person inspires you.
Describe a Family Member You Admire. You should say: who this person is, what he or she does, how often you meet, and explain why you admire this person.
Describe Your Best Friend. You should say: who your friend is, how you met, what you usually do together, and explain why this person is your best friend.
Describe a Teacher Who Helped You. You should say: who the teacher is, what subject he or she taught, how the teacher helped you, and explain why you still remember this teacher.
Describe an Interesting Neighbour. You should say: who the neighbour is, how long you have known him or her, what kind of person he or she is, and explain why you find this neighbour interesting.
Describe a Person You Enjoy Spending Time With. You should say: who the person is, how you know the person, what you usually do together, and explain why you enjoy spending time together.

Describe a Person Who Has Good Communication Skills. You should say: who the person is, how you know him or her, what makes the person a good communicator, and explain what you have learned from this person.
Describe a Polite Person You Know. You should say: who the person is, how you know him or her, how the person behaves, and explain why you think the person is polite.
Describe a Successful Person You Admire. You should say: who the person is, how you know about him or her, what the person has achieved, and explain why you admire this person.

title: IELTS P2 - 14 Places and Travel Questions
questions: Describe a journey that didn’t go as planned. You should say: where you were going, how you were travelling, who you were with, what went wrong, and explain what you would do differently.
Describe a place that you find peaceful. You should say: where it is, when you first went there, what you do there, and why you like it.
Describe a place you have recently visited. You should say: where you went, who you went with, how you got there, and explain why you enjoyed it.
Describe a place near water. You should say: where it is, how you get there, how often you do there, what you can do there, and explain why you like it.
Describe a place with animals. You should say: where it is, how you heard of it, what animals can be seen, and explain why it might be an interesting place to visit.
Describe Your Hometown. You should say: where it is, what it is famous for, what you like about it, and explain why it is special to you.
Describe Your Favourite Place. You should say: where it is, how often you visit it, what you usually do there, and explain why it is your favourite place.
Describe a Memorable Trip. You should say: where you went, who you travelled with, what you did there, and explain why the trip was memorable.
Describe a Historical Place You Visited. You should say: what the place is, where it is located, when you visited it, and explain why it impressed you.
Describe an Interesting Animal. You should say: what the animal is, where you saw it, what it looks like, and explain why you find it interesting.
Describe a Crowded Place You Have Been To. You should say: where the place was, when you went there, why it was crowded, and explain how you felt about being there.
Describe a Dream Travel Destination. You should say: where you would like to go, what you know about the place, who you would like to go with, and explain why you want to visit it.
Describe a Public Building You Like. You should say: what the building is, where it is, what people do there, and explain why you like it.
Describe your favourite shop. You should say: where it is, how often you go there, what it sells, and explain why you think it is a good shop.

title: IELTS P2 - 11 Objects and Media Questions
questions: Describe a piece of art you like. You should say: what the work of art is, when you first saw it, what you know about it, and explain why you like it.
Describe a book you have recently read. You should say: what kind of book it is, what it is about, what sort of people would enjoy it, and explain why you liked it.

Describe a gift you recently gave to someone. You should say: who you gave it to, what kind of person he/she is, what the gift was, what occasion the gift was for, and explain why you chose that gift.
Describe a useful website. You should say: what it is, how often you visit it, what kind of site it is, what kind of information it offers, and explain why you think it is useful.
Describe a song you like. You should say: what kind of song it is, what the song is about, when you first heard it, and explain why you like it.
Describe a photograph you like. You should say: what can be seen in the photo, when it was taken, who took it, and explain why you like it.
Describe a Movie You Recently Watched. You should say: what the movie was, who you watched it with, what it was about, and explain why you liked or disliked it.
Describe a Special Gift You Received. You should say: what the gift was, who gave it to you, on what occasion you received it, and explain why it was special.
Describe a Piece of Technology You Use. You should say: what it is, how long you have used it, what you use it for, and explain why it is important to you.
Describe an Expensive Item You Bought. You should say: what the item was, when you bought it, why you bought it, and explain whether it was worth the money.
Describe a Useful Mobile App. You should say: what the app is, when you started using it, how you use it, and explain why you think it is useful.

title: IELTS P2 - 15 Events and Experiences Questions
questions: Describe a piece of advice you recently received. You should say: when this happened, who gave you the advice, what the advice was, and explain how you felt about the advice.
Describe a time you were embarrassed. You should say: when it was, who you were with, what happened, and how you coped afterwards.
Describe some good news you recently received. You should say: what the news was, how you received the news, who gave it to you, and explain why this was good news.
Describe an unexpected event. You should say: what it was, when it happened, who was there, why it was unexpected, and explain why you enjoyed it.
Describe an Interesting Conversation. You should say: who you talked with, where the conversation took place, what you talked about, and explain why the conversation was interesting.
Describe a Happy Memory. You should say: when it happened, where it happened, who was with you, and explain why it is a happy memory.
Describe an Important Decision You Made. You should say: what the decision was, when you made it, why you made it, and explain how it changed your life.
Describe a Celebration You Attended. You should say: what the celebration was, when and where it took place, who attended it, and explain why you enjoyed it.
Describe a Time You Helped Someone. You should say: who you helped, what happened, how you helped the person, and explain how you felt afterwards.
Describe a Difficult Challenge You Overcame. You should say: what the challenge was, when it happened, how you dealt with it, and explain what you learned from the experience.
Describe a Time You Were Late. You should say: when it happened, why you were late, what happened afterwards, and explain how you felt.
Describe a Goal You Achieved. You should say: what the goal was, how you achieved it, what difficulties you faced, and explain how you felt after achieving it.
Describe a Memorable Meal. You should say: what the meal was, where you had it, who you ate with, and explain why you still remember it.
Describe an Unforgettable Event. You should say: what the event was, when and where it happened, who was with you, and explain why it was unforgettable.
Describe a Difficult Conversation You Had. You should say: who you spoke with, what the conversation was about, why it was difficult, and explain what happened in the end.

title: IELTS P2 - 11 Activities and Learning Questions
questions: Describe a time of the day you like. You should say: what time of day it is, what you do at that time, who you are usually with, and explain why you like it.
Describe an exercise you know. You should say: what it is, how it is done, when you first tried it, what kind of people it is suitable for, and explain why you think it is a good exercise.
Describe an interesting hobby. You should say: what it is, what kind of people do it, how it is done, and explain why you think it is interesting.
Describe a language you have learned. You should say: what it is, when you started learning, how you learned it, what was difficult about it, and why you decided to learn that language.
Describe something you do to relax. You should say: what it is, where you do it, when you first did it, and why you find it relaxing.
Describe a sport you would like to learn. You should say: what it is, what equipment is needed for it, how you would learn it, and explain why you would like to learn this sport.
Describe a Skill You Learned. You should say: what the skill is, how you learned it, how long it took to learn, and explain why the skill is useful.
Describe a Healthy Lifestyle Change You Made. You should say: what the change was, why you decided to make it, how difficult it was, and explain how it has benefited you.
Describe a Subject You Enjoyed Studying. You should say: what the subject was, who taught it, what you learned, and explain why you enjoyed studying it.
Describe an Outdoor Activity You Enjoy. You should say: what the activity is, where you usually do it, who you do it with, and explain why you enjoy it.
Describe a Childhood Game You Enjoyed. You should say: what the game was, who you played with, how the game was played, and explain why you enjoyed it.

title: IELTS P2 - 6 Society and Culture Questions
questions: Describe a good law. You should say: what it is, who is affected by it, and why you think it is good.
Describe a vocation you think is useful to society. You should say: what it is, what it involves, what kind of people usually do this work, and explain why you think it is useful to society.
Describe a Festival You Enjoy. You should say: what the festival is, how people celebrate it, who you celebrate it with, and explain why you enjoy it.
Describe a Foreign Culture You Would Like to Learn About. You should say: which culture it is, what you know about it, why it interests you, and explain why you would like to learn more about it.
Describe a Team Project You Worked On. You should say: what the project was, who worked with you, what your responsibilities were, and explain what you learned from the experience.
Describe an Important Tradition in Your Country. You should say: what the tradition is, when people follow it, why it is important, and explain how it has changed over time.
